name: saas
title: SaaS kit — tenancy, activity, admin projection
description: The framework-independent backend of the Lunora SaaS kit: per-tenant tables sharded by organizationId (projects, activity), a .global() organizations projection for the cross-tenant reads a shard cannot serve, an identity claim contract carrying the caller's active organization, and the queries/mutations the dashboard and admin run on. Identity itself stays in better-auth; this item never becomes a second source of truth for it.
docs: Re-export lunora/saas/index.ts from your lunora/ entry so codegen emits api.saas.*. Then wire `resolveIdentity` in your Worker (on defineApp(), in `.extend((env) => ({ resolveIdentity }))` after `.auth(...)`) to return { userId, activeOrganizationId, orgRole, appRole } from the better-auth session and the caller's member row — the snippet is in lunora/identity.ts, and without it every org-scoped function fails closed with UNPROCESSABLE. Gate shards with `authorizeShard` (the caller's active organization and `__root__` only), and have clients pass `{ shardKey: organizationId }` — read from `api.saas.me` on the root shard — on every org-scoped call. Enable better-auth's organization() and admin() plugins in lunora/auth/index.ts, and call internal.saas.syncOrganization from the organization plugin's organizationHooks (via createShardClient(env.SHARD)) so the admin projection stays in step. `saas_organizations` is a `.global()` table, so chain `.global({ d1: (env) => env.DB })` onto `defineApp()` beside `.shard(...)` — the `auth` item already declares that D1 binding, and without the chain every admin list and slug lookup throws INTERNAL at runtime while the types compile.
